terra.problem: The text does not say the two sides had been pretending to get along or that the three years were quiet.
The text says the leaders treated Abimelech deceitfully, not that both sides treated each other with deceit.
The text does not say how fast the news traveled.
The text does not say that plenty of people heard about the ambush.
The text does not say the report set up everything that followed.
The main-dish comparison uses food imagery other than cookies.
The text does not say there was cheering that turned to cursing. It also does not establish that the festival was exactly three years into Abimelech's reign.
Judges 9:6 says the leaders made Abimelech king, not that they crowned him.
The closing observation about a clear schedule is flat for a moment that has room for Papa Dorin's personality.
Zebul does tell Abimelech to lie in wait, so saying waiting isn't in the message contradicts the plan.
The text does not say Zebul knows exactly who is coming.
The text does not give Zebul's reason for saying this. Marking the proposed reason as a guess does not make it permissible.
The text does not say Abimelech learned from the earlier ambush or that it was why he set up another.
The text says Abimelech and the companies with him took the gate; it does not say one company took it.
Calling the branch-cutting a tree-chopping lesson makes light of preparation for the fatal attack on the people in the chamber.
The men each cut a branch and follow Abimelech, but the text does not say they also lift their branches to their shoulders.
The text does not establish that the millstone was heavier than a clay jar.
